profile.headline: Software engineer and build system specialist
profile.summary: I'm a software developer interested in system design, user interface architecture, programming languages, and how the three work together. I care about why things are the way they are, and how tooling and knowledge sharing can have an impact on communities.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: I am a WebKit <https://webkit.org> contributor and reviewer at Apple. My main areas of focus are on developer tools, build system engineering, and performance.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I build UI frameworks, developer tools, and continuous integration systems to empower other engineers as part of Yelp's Core iOS team. I think holistically about app architecture and its pertinence to developer experience, mentoring other engineers and sharing findings along the way.

My contributions at Yelp have focused specifically on:

• Architecting and implementing a modular build cache, building on top of open source and Apple-provided infrastructure to reduce compile times and improve developer productivity.
• Creating and maintaining a UI framework in use by all iOS teams, making it easier to build powerful, reusable user interfaces while reducing complex mutable state and increasing native UI abstraction.

positions.title: OpenMRS.org Identity Systems Manager
positions.description: I was a volunteer project manager for OpenMRS, an open-source electronic medical record platform. I oversaw development of community and infrastructural applications that OpenMRS uses to coordinate a large community of developers, users, and clinicians.

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description: I taught and assisted students in CS 240, Purdue's C Programming course. Students in CS 240 learn fundamentals of C and systems-level programming, and I helped clarify and guide their experience.

positions.title: Google Code-in Mentor
positions.description:
Mentored a number of high-school-age students who learned about software development and the open-source process by contributing to OpenMRS. Students working for my project learned how to do UI development in a modern web application. Their work contributed to an in-process UI redesign for OpenMRS ID and is running in production at id.openmrs.org as of OpenMRS ID v2.1

Being a mentor helped me learn how better to teach, and how to work with multiple students all at once. I am a better project manager and communicator as a result of Google Code-in.

positions.title: Google Summer of Code Mentor
positions.description:
I mentored an undergraduate student in the 2014 season of Google Summer of Code while working for OpenMRS. This meant I collaborated with and advised the student during the summer as we developed a major version of our OpenMRS ID platform and transitioned the back-end of our platform. I gained experience collaborating on software and managing the work of another contributor.

I was selected from around 30 OpenMRS mentors to represent the organization at Google's Summer of Code Reunion conference in San Jose, California.

positions.title: Community Infrastructure Developer
positions.description: Development, design, and operations management for OpenMRS's web properties. Part of a team writing & maintaining web applications used worldwide by hundreds of developers, implementers, and contributors working to improve our open-source healthcare platform.
